motivation.observed: The Android host shell reports emulator PID 7038 SIGSEGV at 16:35:51.9332966 UTC. This is reporting time, not a measured crash instant. The current bounded Crashpad collector retained only a 40-byte settings.dat; no dump or stack was supplied. This helper seeks an already-saved systemd summary without requesting core contents or changing host core policy.

sources.role: New Linux QA CI process snapshot and bounded saved-journal summary reader
Actual helper execution against synthetic proc/journal fixtures and controlled real child processes

snapshot.placement: After the emulator has booted and before required Maestro flows; root owns exact runner integration.
guards: Linux, CI=true, QA environment, numeric current GitHub run ID, positive PID and launch within the last two hours
Current UID owns the opened /proc/PID directory and all four reported process UID fields match
Executable is one of three explicit canonical SDK emulator/QEMU paths, executable regular file owned by current UID or root; open process target device/inode match the expected file
Live process state; start ticks, UID and executable checked around reads; boot ID read before and after
Owned fixed logs directory; no-follow regular bounded inputs, no linked snapshot reuse and exclusive 0600 output
retainedIdentity: canonical executable path, device and inode
process start ticks and ticks per second

correctness: One noninteractive read-only query, no fallback query or permission modification
A current-run, same-boot snapshot is required; a live reused PID or changed executable is rejected; an absent process is expected after a crash
Every returned record is independently checked for exact crashed-process identity, message ID, boot, signal and microsecond crash timestamp inside the exact launch-to-collection window
JSON duplicate keys, malformed/array identity fields and out-of-window records are rejected; fields outside the allowlist are discarded including journal cursor
MESSAGE is bounded by UTF-8 byte length; missing message is explicitly recorded; multiple matching records remain ambiguous
Raw stdout/stderr are not persisted; numeric result and byte counts remain; permission, missing-tool, timeout, malformed, partial and no-record outcomes are explicit
Original gate exit is recorded, never converted into acceptance; the root runner retains its original required-flow/evidence/decoder result
collection.privilegedReadAuthorization: Root approved the single fixed sudo -n journal read in the existing disposable CI runner; it does not install a handler, request credentials or change permission/core policy.

bounds.rationale: The elevated timeout supervises its own journal child. Python also bounds pipe reads and controlled child shutdown; the caller's three-second timeout covers blocking OS operations. No retry or unbounded debugger/core command is used.

focusedResult.outputRetention: Structured result reconstructed from the observed tool TAP output; full TAP text is in conversation tool output, not claimed as a retained raw file.

static.command: Python ast.parse of the helper source (no bytecode write)

scopes: Actual helper snapshot/collect CLI and file guards execute against a synthetic current-UID proc/SDK tree
Journal selection tests use controlled JSON records and a substituted query boundary; no local sudo or journalctl command ran
Real subprocess reader tests execute harmless Python children for output caps, normal completion, a stall and ignored SIGTERM
The 47 formal Node count includes 20 top-level cases and nested guard cases; it is one owner run, not 47 native workflows
deferred: Native owner independently reviews the frozen helper and runs only the focused file
Root owns combined runner/provenance integration gates
Actual current CI systemd journal/tool permissions, saved crash availability and native outcomes remain unverified

primaryReferences.usedFor: Process start ticks are field 22, measured since boot in clock ticks.
Exact field matches, boot/time filtering, bounded line selection and explicit JSON field selection; --all permits long requested MESSAGE values before our byte caps.
Coredump message ID, crashed-process COREDUMP_PID/UID/EXE fields, microsecond COREDUMP_TIMESTAMP, and optional saved backtrace in MESSAGE.
Trusted _PID/_UID/_EXE describe the logging process, so they are not used as crashed-process identifiers.
The current inventory lists systemd-coredump, but the inspected inventory image differs from the failed job image; this does not establish runtime availability or handler activation.

limits: This is a prepared CI-only diagnostic, not a repair for the emulator crash and not native or movie acceptance.
No current b5 native artifact contains this new snapshot or journal output.

A journal record does not contain the captured process-start-ticks field. Matching boot, PID, UID, executable and launch interval improves attribution but cannot prove start-ticks equality or exclude an unobserved intervening reuse.
A matching backtrace may identify a faulting component; it does not by itself establish why that component failed.

The current root integration collects after emulator shutdown. Any matching crash must be interpreted against the retained pre-cleanup/cleanup chronology; the helper does not label it the original UI failure.

No matching saved record can reflect missing tools, permission denial, disabled/unsupported crash handling, pending systemd processing, or no saved record; absence does not prove the emulator did not crash.
The helper requests no core image, environment, command-line or mapped-library field; it does not scan arbitrary host paths, dump memory, enable core collection, run GDB or change sysctl/ulimit.
The MESSAGE text is systemd-produced diagnostic text and may include a stack summary. Only the explicit fields and bounded message are persisted.
The initial focused tool TAP output was observed directly; this receipt retains its structured result and exact source hashes rather than claiming a separately retained raw TAP file.
